purpose: Diagnose the shared below-random ranking on the held-out southern F4 block without converting association into a causal explanation.

inputs.probabilities: arithmetic four-seed ensembles from accepted V4.2 weighted inference

analyses.feature_shift: train versus test standardized mean shift and two-sample KS statistic for all 32 channels
analyses.class_association: per-role feature ROC AUC and standardized positive-minus-negative mean contrast
analyses.association_reversal: train and test AUC directions on opposite sides of 0.5; material when both absolute departures from 0.5 are at least 0.05
analyses.model_score_association: test-set Spearman correlation of ensemble score with row, column, and each normalized channel
analyses.spatial_dispersion: descriptive metrics in fixed 50-row (5 km) test blocks beginning at row 1250
coordinate_controls: balanced linear logistic regression on standardized row and column
balanced degree-2 polynomial logistic regression on standardized row and column

interpretation_boundaries: KS p-values are descriptive because pixels are spatially dependent.
Twelve 5 km row blocks are descriptive spatial dispersion units, not independent geographic replicates.
Feature-association sign reversals support dataset shift but do not identify a causal environmental mechanism.
Coordinate-control performance indicates spatial confounding risk but does not partition causal effects.
No concealed-fault or new-fault claim is permitted.
